title.fa: روانکاوی نه اعتراف است نه تلقین
title.en: Analysis is neither confession nor suggestion
title.nl: Analysis is neither confession nor suggestion

summary.fa: «محقق بی‌طرف» دو تعبیر آشنا پیش می‌گذارد: این همان اعتراف کلیسایی است، یا همان هیپنوتیزم و تلقین. فروید هر دو را رد می‌کند و در هر دو مورد یک تفاوت دقیق می‌گذارد — تفاوتی که روش کار را تعیین می‌کند.
summary.en: The impartial person offers two familiar readings: this is church confession, or it is hypnosis and suggestion. Freud rejects both and in each case draws a precise distinction — one that determines how the work is done.
summary.nl: The impartial person offers two familiar readings: this is church confession, or it is hypnosis and suggestion. Freud rejects both and in each case draws a precise distinction — one that determines how the work is done.

text.fa: اعتراض اول: «این در حقیقت اساس همان مسئلهٔ اعتراف است، همان چیزی که کلیسای کاتولیک برای تأمین نفوذ معنوی خود بر روح دیگران ظرف مدتی طولانی آن را حفظ کرده است.»
text.en: The first objection: "this is in fact the basis of confession, the very thing the Catholic Church has long maintained to secure its spiritual influence over others’ souls."
text.nl: The first objection: "this is in fact the basis of confession, the very thing the Catholic Church has long maintained to secure its spiritual influence over others’ souls."

text.fa: پاسخ فروید: «پاسخ شما هم مثبت است و هم منفی. اعتراف در روانکاوی هست، ولی تنها به‌عنوان سرآغاز آن… در مسئلهٔ اعتراف گناهکار آنچه را که می‌داند بیان می‌کند؛ اما در روانکاوی بیمار باید بیش از آنچه می‌داند بیان کند.»
text.en: Freud’s answer: "your answer is both yes and no. Confession is present in analysis, but only as its beginning… in confession the sinner tells what he knows; in analysis the patient must tell more than he knows."
text.nl: Freud’s answer: "your answer is both yes and no. Confession is present in analysis, but only as its beginning… in confession the sinner tells what he knows; in analysis the patient must tell more than he knows."

text.fa: و یک نکتهٔ شاهدی: «شاهد و مدرکی در دست نیست که نشان دهد اعترافات کلیسایی قدرت درمان بیمار و برطرف کردن آثار و علائم بیماری را داشته باشند.»
text.en: And a point about evidence: "there is no evidence that church confessions have the power to cure a patient or remove the signs and symptoms of illness."
text.nl: And a point about evidence: "there is no evidence that church confessions have the power to cure a patient or remove the signs and symptoms of illness."

text.fa: اعتراض دوم: پس شاید نفوذ شخصی روانکاو، که به‌خاطر مدت درازتر و رابطهٔ نزدیک‌تر از نفوذ کشیش بیشتر است، یک رابطهٔ هیپنوتیکی و تلقینی می‌سازد و «معجزهٔ روش درمانی شما بر اثر نتایج هیپنوتیزم و تلقین به وجود می‌آید» — به‌علاوه، هیپنوتیزم در مدتی بسیار کمتر از ماه‌ها و سال‌های روانکاوی کار می‌کند.
text.en: The second objection: perhaps the analyst’s personal influence, greater than a priest’s because of the longer time and closer relation, creates a hypnotic and suggestive bond, so that "the miracle of your treatment comes about through the effects of hypnosis and suggestion" — and besides, hypnosis works in far less time than analysis’s months and years.
text.nl: The second objection: perhaps the analyst’s personal influence, greater than a priest’s because of the longer time and closer relation, creates a hypnotic and suggestive bond, so that "the miracle of your treatment comes about through the effects of hypnosis and suggestion" — and besides, hypnosis works in far less time than analysis’s months and years.

text.fa: پاسخ فروید دو بخش دارد. اول اقرار: «چنین نفوذ ویژه‌ای البته وجود دارد و نقش بزرگی هم در مسئلهٔ روانکاوی بر عهده می‌گیرد، اما نه همان نقشی که هیپنوتیزم انجام می‌دهد.» دوم تفکیک: «ما از این نفوذ شخصی آن‌طور که در هیپنوتیزم نیروی تلقین را برای از بین بردن آثار رنج‌آور بیماری به کار می‌برند استفاده نمی‌کنیم.»
text.en: Freud’s answer has two parts. First an admission: "such a special influence certainly exists and plays a large part in analysis, but not the part that hypnosis plays." Then the distinction: "we do not use this personal influence as hypnosis uses the force of suggestion to remove the distressing signs of illness."
text.nl: Freud’s answer has two parts. First an admission: "such a special influence certainly exists and plays a large part in analysis, but not the part that hypnosis plays." Then the distinction: "we do not use this personal influence as hypnosis uses the force of suggestion to remove the distressing signs of illness."

text.fa: و تصریح می‌کند که این نفوذ عامل اصلی نیست: «اشتباه است اگر فکر کنیم این نیرو همان عامل اصلی کار ماست و پیشرفت اساسی درمان را باعث می‌شود. در آغاز کار همین‌طور است ولی بعداً به‌عنوان کمکی برای اجرای روانکاوی به کار خواهد رفت» — و در نهایت به کار «بزرگ‌ترین عمل ضدتلقینی» می‌آید.
text.en: And he insists this influence is not the main agent: "it is a mistake to think this force is the chief factor in our work and what brings about the essential progress of the cure. At the start it is, but later it serves as an aid to carrying out the analysis" — and in the end it serves "the greatest anti-suggestive act."
text.nl: And he insists this influence is not the main agent: "it is a mistake to think this force is the chief factor in our work and what brings about the essential progress of the cure. At the start it is, but later it serves as an aid to carrying out the analysis" — and in the end it serves "the greatest anti-suggestive act."

text.fa: مثال عملی تفاوت، در مورد احساس گناه: اگر بیمار از احساس ارتکاب گناه رنج می‌برد، «به او توصیه نمی‌کنیم که چون بی‌شک بی‌گناه هستی پس وسوسه‌های وجدان اخلاقی خود را کنار بگذار. این کاری است که خود به آن عمل کرده و نتیجه‌ای هم نگرفته است.»
text.en: A practical example of the difference, in the case of guilt: if the patient suffers from a sense of having committed a crime, "we do not advise him that since he is surely innocent he should set aside the promptings of his conscience. That is what he has already tried, without result."
text.nl: A practical example of the difference, in the case of guilt: if the patient suffers from a sense of having committed a crime, "we do not advise him that since he is surely innocent he should set aside the promptings of his conscience. That is what he has already tried, without result."

text.fa: و جایگزینش: «برایش تشریح می‌کنیم که این چنین احساس نیرومند و مداوم می‌بایستی از یک مسئلهٔ دیگری سرچشمه گرفته باشد که شاید ما بتوانیم آن را کشف کنیم» — یعنی علامت را انکار نمی‌کند، سرچشمه‌اش را جابه‌جا می‌کند.
text.en: And its replacement: "we explain to him that so strong and persistent a feeling must spring from something else, which we may perhaps be able to discover" — the symptom is not denied; its source is relocated.
text.nl: And its replacement: "we explain to him that so strong and persistent a feeling must spring from something else, which we may perhaps be able to discover" — the symptom is not denied; its source is relocated.

text.fa: هر دو تفکیک، ادعای فروید دربارهٔ کار خودش است و در این رساله شاهد تجربی برایشان نمی‌آورد؛ اثربخشی روانکاوی در سنجش با دارونما و با درمان‌های دیگر پرسشی است که یک قرن بعد هم باز است.
text.en: Both distinctions are Freud’s claims about his own practice, and he offers no empirical evidence for them in this essay; whether analysis works compared with placebo and with other therapies is a question still open a century later.
text.nl: Both distinctions are Freud’s claims about his own practice, and he offers no empirical evidence for them in this essay; whether analysis works compared with placebo and with other therapies is a question still open a century later.
